title: Birth outcomes of cohabiting and non-cohabiting minors and young adults in Argentina, 2001-2021: a population-based register study.
authors: Alazraqui M, Trotta A, Guevel CG, Godoy MP, Mignone J, Juárez SP, Urquia ML.
abstract: Background Maternal age and cohabitation (women living with a partner in marriage or in a common-law relationship) are known to be associated with adverse birth outcomes. However, how these two factors jointly contribute to birth outcomes is not well understood, particularly among minor mothers. Methods All live births that occurred in Argentina 2001-2021 (N=13 807 028) were used to estimate the prevalence of births to minor mothers ( Results Minor mothers accounted for 6% of all births (n=791 731), lived in poor regions and were more likely to have incomplete primary education and no employment. Among mothers aged Conclusions The cohabitation advantage among young adults was not observed among minor mothers, particularly those aged ≤15 years.
